name.en: Fake ATO or myGov message: “sign in to fix your tax”

how.en: Around tax time you get a text, email or call that looks like it is from the Australian Taxation Office or myGov, with official logos. It says something is urgent and asks you to sign in through a link, open an attachment or call a number. The link goes to a fake myGov page that steals your sign-in details, which scammers then use to commit fraud in your name. The ATO never sends a link asking you to sign in.

text.en: A text, email or call claims to be from the ATO or myGov, with official logos.
It says you must act now about a refund, a debt or your account.
It asks you to sign in to myGov through a link or call a number.
The fake page takes your sign-in details and scammers use them to commit fraud in your name.
myGov: Your tax refund of $746.20 is on hold. Verify your details within 24 hours to release it: [link]

en: An unexpected message from the ATO with a link. The ATO never does this.
A link that asks you to sign in to myGov.
The sender’s address does not end in .gov.au.
Pressure to act quickly about a refund or a debt.
Don’t click the link. Sign in to myGov by typing the address yourself or using the official app.
Check with the ATO using its official app, website or phone number.
If you shared your details, contact the ATO quickly to protect your accounts.
